item.title: BAE Systems cybersecurity incident disrupts US Federal Bankruptcy Noticing Center nationwide
item.description:
Government IT services incident updates confirm nationwide operational disruptions affecting federal court communications. Unauthenticated threat actors compromised infrastructure hosting official noticing and bankruptcy communication networks, forcing system administrators to sever public connectivity.
The cyber incident impacted the US Federal Bankruptcy Noticing Center BNC managed under federal technology contracting services by BAE Systems. Threat actors accessed internal network segments, disrupting automated court mailing operations, electronic noticing gateways, and administrative case filing systems nationwide. Federal judiciary IT teams and forensic contractors initiated emergency containment protocols to isolate core databases and verify whether sensitive case filings were exfiltrated during the intrusion.
Subverting government technology contractors highlights critical supply chain dependencies in judicial IT operations. When central service providers suffer system outages or security breaches, core public sector functions encounter immediate operational downtime, delaying legal notices and compromising administrative processing.
- Conduct immediate network segmentation audits across government service portals and third-party contractor interfaces. - Enforce strict out-of-band identity verification for all automated administrative workflows connecting to federal databases. - Inspect system access logs for anomalous remote desktop connections or unverified service account activity. - Verify off-site backup integrity and maintain isolated, immutable system recovery images for critical administrative databases.
Government service supply chain security demands continuous vendor risk monitoring and robust network isolation to ensure critical public infrastructure remains resilient against unauthorized intrusion attempts. #CodeDefence #BAESystems #JudiciarySecurity #GovernmentIT #SupplyChain #IncidentResponse #AppSec #DataProtection

item.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup identity breach allowed malwareless access to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants
item.description:
Threat intelligence research published today details architectural vulnerabilities in delegated cloud application trust relationships. Threat actors leveraged compromised vendor identity credentials to execute malwareless data exfiltration operations across client cloud organizations.
The supply chain incident involved stolen application credentials associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup formerly SkyKick. Unauthenticated remote adversaries utilized valid administrative service tokens to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID formerly Azure Active Directory endpoints. Because client tenants granted persistent delegated administrative access to the vendor application, adversaries executed legitimate API calls to query user directories, download Exchange Online mailboxes, and inspect SharePoint repositories across 173 enterprise cloud environments without dropping local malware binaries.
Relying on persistent delegated administrative permissions creates severe cloud supply chain exposure. When a third-party vendor application credential is compromised, adversaries can ride existing OAuth consent grants directly into customer tenant environments without triggering multi-factor authentication or password reset barriers.
- Revoke all delegated administrative privileges and active OAuth tokens associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup immediately. - Enforce granular, time-bound Partner Admin relationships granular delegated admin privileges GDAP across all tenant environments. - Audit Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs for high-volume service principal API calls originating from unverified external IP addresses. - Restrict OAuth application consent policies to require explicit administrator approval for multi-tenant application requests.
Cloud identity governance requires continuous partner permission auditing and strict non-human identity monitoring to ensure enterprise cloud tenants remain protected against supply chain credential abuse. #CodeDefence #ConnectWise #Microsoft365 #EntraID #SupplyChain #IdentitySecurity #CloudSecurity #AppSec

item.title: Nextcloud CODE server vulnerability exploited in the wild to plant persistent web shell backdoors
item.description:
Web application security writeups published today confirm active wild exploitation targeting self-hosted cloud storage environments. Threat actors weaponized input validation flaws in document editing extensions to write arbitrary executable files into public web hosting roots.
The vulnerability impacts Nextcloud instances running the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server extension. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed HTTP queries to bypass path sanitization subroutines, executing arbitrary code and dropping persistent PHP web shell backdoors into hosting directories. Threat telemetry indicates automated scanning toolkits actively locating exposed Nextcloud installations to upload web shell implants and establish persistent server access.
Subverting cloud storage application servers exposes proprietary documents, user credentials, and internal filesystems. Possessing unauthenticated web shell access on self-hosted cloud storage nodes allows adversaries to exfiltrate user files, manipulate local database records, and execute lateral movement sweeps across internal networks.
- Upgrade the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server extension or Nextcloud core installation immediately to current patched builds. - Remove the Built-in CODE Server extension on unpatched instances where emergency updates cannot be applied immediately. - Inspect web server hosting directories for newly created PHP files or unexpected script modifications created during recent windows. - Configure web application firewalls to inspect incoming HTTP requests for directory traversal patterns and malformed PHP payloads.
Cloud application platform security depends on strict input sanitization and rapid extension patch maintenance to ensure self-hosted data repositories remain protected against web shell backdoors. #CodeDefence #Nextcloud #Collabora #WebShell #RCE #CloudSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #WebSecurity
